entities.name: Gautier de Coincy
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Gautier de Coincy (1177–1236) emerged as a pivotal figure in early 13th-century French culture, renowned as an abbot, a skilled trouvère, and a master of musical arrangement. Born in Coincy, Picardy, his profound devotion to the Virgin Mary defined his artistic output, culminating in his monumental work, *Les Miracles de Nostre Dame*. This collection of some 30,000 lines of verse, interwoven with 114 original songs and contrafacta (new texts set to existing melodies), solidified his place as a key innovator in the burgeoning vernacular literary and musical traditions of the High Middle Ages, bridging sacred themes with courtly aesthetics.

Throughout his ecclesiastical career, Gautier served as prior of the priory of St. Médard at Coincy and later as abbot of the Benedictine monastery of Saint-Sauveur de Vic-sur-Aisne from 1214 to 1233, before becoming abbot of Saint Médard de Soissons until his death. His *Miracles de Nostre Dame* was not merely a compilation of Marian legends but a vibrant, personal testament to the Virgin's intercessory power, drawing on a rich tapestry of miracles, hymns, and moralistic tales. Unlike many contemporaries, Gautier meticulously indicated the musical settings for his poems, either composing new melodies or adapting popular secular tunes, thereby creating a unique synthesis of spiritual narrative and accessible, engaging music.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Gautier de Coincy's *Miracles de Nostre Dame* profoundly influenced the cult of the Virgin Mary in medieval France, solidifying her veneration through accessible vernacular poetry and music. His work served as a crucial bridge between sacred themes and popular culture, setting a precedent for religious lyrical expression.
